questions.problem:
Which of the following statements are logically equivalent?

I. $A∧B$

II. $A∧(B∨¬A)$

III. $¬(¬B∨¬A)$
questions.worked_solution:
Two statements are logically equivalent if they have the same truth table. So, we construct a truth table for the three given statements:

| $\,A\,$ | $\,B\,$ | $\,A∧B\,$ | $\,A∧(B∨¬A)\,$ | $\,¬(¬B∨¬A)\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ |

We see that the statements $A∧B,\,$ $A∧(B∨¬A)$ and $¬(¬B∨¬A)$ have the same truth table, so they are logically equivalent.

Therefore, the correct answer is "I, II, and III".

questions.problem:
Which of the following statements are logically equivalent?

I. $¬P∨(P∧Q)$

II. $¬P∨Q$

III. $¬P∨¬Q$
questions.worked_solution:
Two statements are logically equivalent if they have the same truth table. So, we construct a truth table for the three given statements:

| $\,P\,$ | $\,Q\,$ | $\,¬P∨(P∧Q)\,$ | $\,¬P∨Q\,$ | $\,¬P∨¬Q\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ |

We see that only the statements $¬P∨(P∧Q)$ and $¬P∨Q$ have the same truth table, so they are logically equivalent.

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and II only".

questions.problem:
Find the missing values in the following truth table:

| $\,P\,$ | $\,Q\,$ | $\,¬P∨¬(Q∨P)\,$ | $\,¬(P∧Q)∨¬P\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | {{field-1}} |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | {{field-2}} | $\text{T}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | {{field-3}} |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ |

Using your results, complete the following statement:

$$
¬P∨¬(Q∨P){{field-4}}¬(P∧Q)∨¬P
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, let's solve for the missing values:

- When $P≡\text{T}$ and $Q≡\text{T},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}¬(P∧Q)∨¬P & ≡¬(\text{T}∧\text{T})∨¬\text{T} \\  & ≡¬\text{T}∨\text{F} \\  & ≡\text{F}∨\text{F} \\  & ≡\text{F}\end{aligned}
$$

- When $P≡\text{T}$ and $Q≡\text{F},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}¬P∨¬(Q∨P) & ≡¬\text{T}∨¬(\text{F}∨\text{T}) \\  & ≡\text{F}∨¬\text{T} \\  & ≡\text{F}∨\text{F} \\  & ≡\text{F}\end{aligned}
$$

- When $P≡\text{F}$ and $Q≡\text{T},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}¬(P∧Q)∨¬P & ≡¬(\text{F}∧\text{T})∨¬\text{F} \\  & ≡¬\text{F}∨\text{T} \\  & ≡\text{T}∨\text{T} \\  & ≡\text{T}\end{aligned}
$$

Our completed table is shown below.

| $\,P\,$ | $\,Q\,$ | $\,¬P∨¬(Q∨P)\,$ | $\,¬(P∧Q)∨¬P\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ |

To determine whether $¬P∨¬(Q∨P)$ is logically equivalent to $¬(P∧Q)∨¬P,$ we need to check whether their truth tables are equivalent.

Looking at the last two columns, we see that they differ in the second row. Therefore, we conclude that 

$$
¬P∨¬(Q∨P)≢¬(P∧Q)∨¬P.
$$

questions.problem:
Find the missing values in the following truth table:

| $\,P\,$ | $\,Q\,$ | $\,P∨¬(Q∨P)\,$ | $\,(¬P∧¬Q)∨P\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | {{field-1}} | $\text{T}$ |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | {{field-2}} |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | {{field-3}} |

Using your results, complete the following statement:

$$
P∨¬(Q∨P){{field-4}}(¬P∧¬Q)∨P
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, let's solve for the missing values:

- When $P≡\text{T}$ and $Q≡\text{T},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P∨¬(Q∨P) & ≡\text{T}∨¬(\text{T}∨\text{T}) \\  & ≡\text{T}∨\text{F} \\  & ≡\text{T}\end{aligned}
$$

- When $P≡\text{F}$ and $Q≡\text{T},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}(¬P∧¬Q)∨P & ≡(¬\text{F}∧¬\text{T})∨\text{F} \\  & ≡(\text{T}∧\text{F})∨\text{F} \\  & ≡\text{F}∨\text{F} \\  & ≡\text{F}\end{aligned}
$$

- When $P≡\text{F}$ and $Q≡\text{F},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}(¬P∧¬Q)∨P & ≡(¬\text{F}∧¬\text{F})∨\text{F} \\  & ≡(\text{T}∧\text{T})∨\text{F} \\  & ≡\text{T}∨\text{F} \\  & ≡\text{T}\end{aligned}
$$

Our completed table is shown below.

| $\,P\,$ | $\,Q\,$ | $\,P∨¬(Q∨P)\,$ | $\,(¬P∧¬Q)∨P\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ |

To determine whether $P∨¬(Q∨P)$ is logically equivalent to $(¬P∧¬Q)∨P,$ we need to check whether their truth tables are equivalent.  

Looking at the last two columns, we see that they are the same $(\text{T},\text{T},\text{F},\text{T}).$ Therefore, we conclude that 

$$
P∨¬(Q∨P)≡(¬P∧¬Q)∨P.

questions.problem:
Find the missing values in the following truth table:

| $\,P\,$ | $\,Q\,$ | $\,P∨(Q∧¬(P∧¬Q))\,$ | $\,P∨Q\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | {{field-1}} | $\text{T}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | {{field-2}} |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | {{field-3}} |

Using your results, complete the following statement:

$$
P∨(Q∧¬(P∧¬Q)){{field-4}}P∨Q
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, let's solve for the missing values:

- When $P≡\text{T}$ and $Q≡\text{F},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P∨(Q∧¬(P∧¬Q)) & ≡\text{T}∨(\text{F}∧¬(\text{T}∧¬\text{F})) \\  & ≡\text{T}∨(\text{F}∧¬(\text{T}∧\text{T})) \\  & ≡\text{T}∨(\text{F}∧¬\text{T}) \\  & ≡\text{T}∨(\text{F}∧\text{F}) \\  & ≡\text{T}∨\text{ }\text{F} \\  & ≡\text{T}\end{aligned}
$$

- When $P≡\text{F}$ and $Q≡\text{T},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P∨Q & ≡\text{F}∨\text{T} \\  & ≡\text{T}\end{aligned}
$$

- When $P≡\text{F}$ and $Q≡\text{F},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P∨Q & ≡\text{F}∨\text{F} \\  & ≡\text{F}\end{aligned}
$$

Our completed table is shown below.  

| $\,P\,$ | $\,Q\,$ | $\,P∨(Q∧¬(P∧¬Q))\,$ | $\,P∨Q\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ |

To determine whether $P∨(Q∧¬(P∧¬Q))$ is logically equivalent to $P∨Q,$ we need to check whether their truth tables are equivalent.

Looking at the last two columns, we see that they are the same $(\text{T},\text{T},\text{T},\text{F}).$ Therefore, we conclude that 

$$
P∨(Q∧¬(P∧¬Q))≡P∨Q.
$$
